summary: Iter 726 (pagination + night-shift fix) tested end-to-end. Backend pytest suite (12 tests) PASSED 100% — monthly-grid pagination (skip=0/limit=5 → 5 rows + total_rows=127; skip=5/limit=5 → non-overlapping page; no-limit → 127 rows and NO total_rows key), single-employee fast path (/admin/employees?user_id=... → 1 row; ?company_id=... → 127 rows), night-shift has_unpaired_punches (recent open IN NOT flagged, 6-day-old lone IN still flagged, normal IN→OUT clean, IN→IN old day still flagged), stitch_cross_day_ot echo-consumption (day1 gains 05:00 OUT, day2 becomes empty; 4-day night-shift regression clean), and dedupe_close_punches import sanity. Frontend UI verified via Playwright with injected super-admin session (post-2FA): (1) /attendance-grid for Kankani renders correctly — Group filter shows 'All (127)', 'LABOUR (108)', 'STAFF (16)'; chunked load produced no visible pagination stutter for 127 rows (single chunk since <150). Month change 2026-08 → 2026-07 reloaded cleanly (July had actual punches, showed correct IN/OUT + missing-punch chips). No stale mixing observed. (2) /employee-master?user_id=<uid> loads the detail page using the NEW fast-path — verified 4 network calls to /api/admin/employees?user_id=... (no full-firm fetch). Name/code/all cards (Grouping, PF-UAN/ESIC, Dummy Shift, Login Credentials, Face, Device Security, Documents/PDF) render with expected testIDs.
critical_code_review_comments: attendance-grid.tsx: chunked loader uses loadSeq guard to avoid stale updates — correct. Fast path 150 rows first + 400-row chunks — good. total_rows fallback to employees.length keeps back-compat.
server.py has_unpaired_punches: 16-hour rolling window correctly protects TODAY's open night shift. Uses datetime.now(UTC) so timezone-safe.
payroll_core.py list_employees: user_id filter is ANDed AFTER company scope + sub_admin scope — safe, cannot bypass RBAC.
employee-master.tsx: reloadDocs uses /admin/employees/{uid}/documents (docs-only endpoint). load() correctly rehydrates full detail on focus without re-fetching firm list.
